A well-formed RFC 3339 timestamp in the future cannot establish an observation made at the measurement time.
RFC 9110 section 8.3 defines Content-Type as a media-type string, not a number.
RFC 9110 section 8.3 defines Content-Type as a media-type string, not an array.
The existing fetch receipt is a control for preserving acceptance of the unmodified round-23 fixture.
RFC 8259 sections 6 and 9 exclude NaN from JSON numbers and a receipt parser must reject the non-JSON token without crashing.
RFC 8259 sections 6 and 9 exclude Infinity from JSON numbers and a receipt parser must reject the non-JSON token without crashing.
RFC 8259 section 4 says object names SHOULD be unique; duplicate receipt keys make the selected value ambiguous and must not be accepted as a valid measurement.
A truncated fetch receipt does not satisfy JSON syntax or provide a complete observation object.
The runner requires claim ids to be unique (measure_c1.py:68-75); RFC 8259 section 5 permits repeated array values but does not override this receipt-level uniqueness rule.
RFC 8259 section 7 permits ] in a string, but the documented literal citation becomes [fire-journal-codes:c1]] and that exact token is not present after the heading.
RFC 8259 section 7 permits an escaped LF in a string, but the documented literal citation includes that decoded LF and does not occur after the heading.
The contract requires the complete [unit:id] literal, so the existing [fire-journal-codes:c1] cannot satisfy id c11; RFC 8259 section 8.3 compares decoded strings rather than prefixes.
RFC 3339 section 5.6 defines time-hour as 2DIGIT ; 00-23, so hour 25 is not a valid date-time; the round-23 prefix test never reads the time part.
RFC 3339 section 5.6 full-time requires a time-offset (Z or numeric), and section 4.4 calls unqualified local time unacceptable for Internet timestamps; the round-23 prefix test accepts it.

RFC 3339 section 5.7 caps February date-mday at 28 (29 in leap years), so 2026-02-30 is not a valid full-date; the round-23 runner rejects it only because '02' sorts before '10', so the impossible day is never tested.
RFC 3339 section 5.6 defines date-month as 2DIGIT ; 01-12; the round-23 prefix test accepts 2026-13-01 because '3' sorts after '0' at the sixth character.
A valid RFC 3339 full-date (section 5.6) dated after the sandbox commit 2026-10-21T12:00:00Z that records it; the lane's own gap statement names future-looking observedAt strings as malformed.

A valid RFC 3339 date-time (section 5.6) 11h59m59s after the committer time 2026-10-21T12:00:00Z that records it; an observation cannot postdate its commit, so the bound must compare instants, not calendar days.

RFC 3339 section 5.6 is built on ABNF DIGIT, defined in RFC 5234 Appendix B.1 as %x30-39 (ASCII 0-9 only); RFC 8259 section 8.1 requires UTF-8 JSON, so the bytes parse and only the date grammar can reject them.
Neither an RFC 3339 full-date nor date-time (section 5.6); the round-23 prefix test accepts it because 'u' sorts after '2'.

Control: the date-only form 2026-10-21 is what all 17 round-23 population receipts carry (an RFC 3339 section 5.6 full-date); the replacement must keep the 17/17 control accepted. The sandbox commit is empty because the value is unchanged.
Control: a valid RFC 3339 date-time (section 5.6, time-offset Z) inside the window and before the committer time 2026-10-21T12:00:00Z.

Control: RFC 3339 section 5.6 NOTE allows lower-case 't' and 'z' (ABNF string literals are case-insensitive, RFC 5234 section 2.3); Python's datetime.fromisoformat rejects this form, so a naive stdlib parse would over-reject.
